stories.headline: CM Sarma calls Akhil Gogoi's flood relief protest 'class V-VI politics'
stories.title: CM Sarma calls Akhil Gogoi's flood relief protest 'class V-VI politics'
stories.summary: The chief minister accused the Sivasagar MLA of seeking political credit for flood relief as Gogoi stages a sit-in protest demanding compensation for affected families
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Guwahati: Today, Raijor Dal president and Sivasagar MLA Akhil Gogoi began an indefinite strike at the Assam Assembly campus, demanding compensation for flood-affected families in Upper Assam and a CBI inquiry into the causes of the devastating floods.
Gogoi launched the protest after paying tribute to Mahatma Gandhi on Gandhi Jayanti.
He had earlier set 1st October as a deadline for the government to complete the distribution of flood relief.
Gogoi is further demanding Rs 10 lakh compensation for every family that suffered major losses in the floods, besides seeking a CBI investigation into the causes and extent of the devastation.
The demands were raised at a public rally at Chachal Dharna Ground in Guwahati on 23rd September.
Gogoi has said the agitation will continue until all eligible flood-affected families receive the assistance being sought.

stories.headline: Congress accuses Election Commission of ‘lying’ about ECINet, demands accountability
stories.title: Congress accuses Election Commission of ‘lying’ about ECINet, demands accountability
stories.summary: Jairam Ramesh alleges the poll body violated the Representation of the People Act by restricting Electoral Registration Officers’ access to the ECINet voter roll system
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Congress on Friday (October 2, 2026) accused the Election Commission of “lying” about the ECINet portal and violating the Representation of the People Act, as it stressed accountability for the “violations of the law and the Constitution.”

Jairam Ramesh, the Congress general secretary in-charge of communications, said that in its “damage control but actually damage enhancing” press note of September 26, 2026, the Election Commission of India had promised a committee to certify that the legally suspect ECINet “complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules.”
“In reality, this should never have been in doubt at all in the first place if the intentions of the CEC Gyanesh Kumar were honest, which they were not,” Mr. Ramesh said.

ECINet was launched on January 22, 2026, with much fanfare, to “enhance transparency, credibility and public trust,” he said in a post on X. The Election Commission’s press note of that day had assured the country the system “has been developed in strict accordance with the law” and in full compliance with the Constitution of India, the Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951, and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, he said.
“All of this was a lie,” Mr. Ramesh claimed.

“By restricting access of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to the ECINet voter roll system and by overruling EROs in states like Goa, West Bengal and others, the ECI controlled by the CEC has violated The Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960,” Mr. Ramesh said, adding that both laws establish that the ERO has statutory authority over the electoral roll.

After the revelations last week, the Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer wrote to the Election Commission on September 24, 2026, asking for a correction of this “illegal state of affairs,” Mr. Ramesh pointed out.

“Starting today, the INDIA janbandhan, citizens and many civil society organisations will hit the streets across the country demanding accountability for these violations of the law and the Constitution,” he said.

The Congress had said on Thursday (October 1, 2026) that the chorus of voices against the “capture” of the electoral system was getting louder, and asserted that citizens would no longer tolerate “vote chori” in any form.

The opposition INDIA bloc had, on Wednesday (September 30, 2026), announced joint “save democracy” marches in all districts and five major rallies, demanded that future polls be held with ballot paper, and appealed to the Supreme Court to expedite cases on the SIR and alleged electoral “malpractices.”

At a meeting attended by leaders of as many as 19 political parties, it was decided that all Opposition MPs would march to the Election Commission on October 6, 2026, and that leaders would meet the President to raise alleged irregularities in the voter list revision.
The grouping also discussed its demand for the CEC’s resignation, saying it would not relent until he was removed.

stories.headline: CJP, student groups to protest, demand Election Commission chief's resignation
stories.title: CJP, student groups to protest, demand Election Commission chief's resignation
stories.summary: A few dozen protesters gathered at the site in Delhi on Friday morning, but police ‌bundled some into buses and took them away, while several nearby metro stations remained shut ‌and security ⁠was tightened.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Prime Minister Narendra Modi faced renewed pressure on Friday as the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party and a separate coalition of student and activist groups stage fresh protests, demanding the resignation of the elections commission chief over a controversial voter roll revision.
The influential CJP will rally in Mumbai and plans to expand demonstrations nationwide in the coming days, while student and civil society groups will gather at New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.

A few dozen protesters gathered at the site in Delhi on Friday morning, but police bundled some into buses and took them away, while several nearby metro stations remained shut and security was tightened.
Officers repeatedly warned against gatherings of more than five people over loudspeakers as hundreds of police and paramilitary personnel surrounded the barricaded protest site.
As police pushed him onto a bus, protester.
Rishabh Singh said, “the right to protest is our fundamental right, and we want answers from the government on vote theft.”
In Mumbai, protesters were expected to gather in the afternoon and hundreds of police were seen assembling around the site.
The protests mark the latest escalation in a dispute that has put unprecedented scrutiny on India’s Election Commission, long regarded as one of the country’s most trusted institutions.
The protesters’ main allegation is that the commission manipulated voter rolls in ways that favour Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The commission and the government have denied the allegations.

Pressure on Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar intensified last month after the Indian Express newspaper reported the election chief’s two deputies had formally raised concerns at least 14 times over the past 10 months over voter-list revisions, registration procedures and the commission’s digital systems.
The Election Commission has said differing views are normal in internal deliberations.
